First release of `omarchy-dms`: use [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org) themes in
[Dank Material Shell](https://danklinux.com) as
[dmsProfiles](https://github.com/satoshoe-dev/dms-profiles) looks, so one picker switches
colors, wallpaper and light/dark mode together.

## What it does

- Converts an Omarchy `colors.toml` into a DMS custom theme, with the previews the DMS
  Browse tab shows. Both Omarchy palette shapes work: the full one and the plain ANSI
  `color0`..`color15` one.
- Copies the theme's wallpapers and creates one dmsProfiles profile per theme.
- Installs themes from the [omarchy.org/themes](https://omarchy.org/themes/) store with one
  command, and keeps track of where each one came from so it can be updated later.
- After a profile switch, points the wallpaper back at the theme's folder so a wallpaper
  carousel lists every image of the theme, not just the profile's copy.

## Commands

```sh
omarchy-dms install [owner/repo]     # install a community theme (no argument: pick from the store)
omarchy-dms installed                # every theme, its origin, and whether it has a profile
omarchy-dms update [theme...]        # refetch installed themes
omarchy-dms remove [-y] [theme...]   # theme, wallpapers and profile
omarchy-dms list                     # repos listed on the store
omarchy-dms sync [--force] [theme...] # profiles for Omarchy's own themes
```

It is also an importable Python library (`omarchy_dms.Omarchy`) that never prints or exits,
so other frontends can use it instead of running the CLI.

## Install

```sh
pipx install omarchy-dms
```

Or with Nix: `nix run github:Villoh/omarchy-dms`.

## Requirements and limits

- Linux with DMS and the dmsProfiles plugin enabled; Python 3.11+ and `git`; `fzf` is optional
  (the pickers).
- Only themes that ship a `colors.toml` work. Alacritty-only themes are rejected with a message.
- Omarchy has no Material color roles, so the conversion to DMS roles is an approximation;
  light themes are the most likely to need tweaks.
- This is an early release. Developed and used on NixOS; reports from other distributions are welcome.
